title: Chain equation for the constructed pinned stalk tensor coordinates
statement: Fix a cartesian square of schemes $X'\xrightarrow{g'}X$, $S'\xrightarrow g S$, $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S'$ and a point $z\in X'$. Use its actual stalk rings $R,A,B,C$ and the scalar-extension functor $F$ and stalk functors of [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Let $P,Q$ be arbitrary complexes on $X$, $N$ an arbitrary complex on $X'$, and $a:H Q\to N$ a chain map, where $H$ is termwise module pullback. Suppose $\chi:H\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(HP\otimes HQ)$ restricts on every total-degree summand to the specified module pullback tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. Write $U=P_{g'z}$, $V=Q_{g'z}$, and $t=\operatorname{tensorStalkIso}(Q);S(a)$, with $S$ the stalk complex functor on $X'$ at $z$. Fix σ to the inverse source pinned stalk tensor isomorphism of [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-stalk-square]. Fix ρ to tensorStalkIso(P) tensor identity followed by the inverse target pinned stalk tensor comparison. For these explicitly constructed σ and ρ the equation F(σ);tensorStalkIso(Tot(P tensor Q));S(χ;(1 tensor a)) = μ_F^{-1};(1 tensor t);ρ holds. This statement verifies the chain equation only; it does not assert existence of coordinate isomorphisms.

proof.text: Fix sigma and rho by the specific isomorphism constructions in the statement, using the proved pinned stalk tensor comparison. Its injection equation is retained for both source and target comparisons. The tensorStalkIso component formula is the inverse canonical module pullback-stalk comparison transported along the stalk ring map equality.

For each total-degree summand, apply the assumed degreewise equation for chi. The generator formulas for the pinned module tensor-pullback map and pullback-stalk comparison, together with the scalar-extension tensorator formula, identify the two composites on each pure tensor with scalar extension of its first factor followed by the stalk of a in its second factor. Pure tensors generate each summand, and the coproduct universal property gives equality in every degree, hence equality of chain maps. Zero rings and zero factors give the unique maps; arbitrary direct sums handle unbounded complexes.
